findings.reason: the followup is the only next-invocation record, and its stated scope omits six implementable sections that no other followup names.
findings.text: the single driving followup is titled "Land §2, then build §3 to §11" while `plan-section-declarations` declares s12–s17 implementable, so the chain a coordinator follows ends six sections short and those sections can be left unbuilt with the followup resolved

findings.reason: two of the three declared negative controls cannot go red at base, and the done-when is weaker than the section's own endpoint, so a worker can pass while long ticks still stretch the bound.
findings.text: two of §13's three criteria hold at the base revision: `StationReloader.poll` (reckon/crew/station.py:831-874) already reloads at the first poll where `_quiet` reports the derivations idle, and already reloads at the first poll after `RELOAD_HOLD_SECONDS` expires, so "fires at the first poll" and "no later than one tick after the bound expires" are true of unfixed code; criterion 1 also accepts a delay of one whole tick, which is the stretch the Why names as the defect

findings.reason: a done-when whose tolerance the implementer picks measures the implementer's choice, so a ten-minute exit bound would pass the §14 gate while the SIGKILL-after-120 s defect stands.
findings.text: §14's tolerance is "within a stated bound" and no bound is stated anywhere in the section, though its own Why supplies the tolerance at 120 s; the same shape recurs at line 164, where §16 reports a run "after a stated number of attempts" without naming the count

findings.reason: a node briefed from this cause bounds two waits that are already bounded and leaves the in-flight tick, the actual reason a stopping station needs SIGKILL, untouched.
findings.text: §14 blames `dispatch_claims.wait_for_dispatches_in_flight` and the `DUTY_DRAIN_SECONDS` duties drain for a SIGTERM ignored for 120 s, but that wait is bounded by `REEXEC_DISPATCH_WAIT_SECONDS = 60.0` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:889) and the drain by `DUTY_DRAIN_SECONDS = 10.0` (reckon/crew/station.py:452), while the stop handler only sets a flag (reckon/crew/station.py:1268) and the loop sits inside an uninterruptible `station.tick()` call
